newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CENBANK SAYS LOST 8.7 BILLION CROWNS IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CENBANK SAYS LOST 8.7 BILLION CROWNS IN 1996.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) said on Thursday that preliminary figures showed the central bank lost 8.7 billion crowns last year due to the creation of reserves, and losses in the value of foreign reserve holdings.
It said in a statement that the firming of the crown's exchange rate in 1996 cost the central bank 8.5 billion crowns in the value of the foreign exchange reserves it held.
The additional creation of reserves and provisions of five billion crowns, also affected the final result, which is still subject to an audit, it said.
The CNB's total yield in 1996 was 43.7 billion crowns against costs of 52.4 billion crowns.
The central bank posted a net profit of 1.002 billion crowns in 1995.
